findings.message: The first replacement in sanitizeDiagnostic uses caret notation (\^@, \^H, \^_) as if it were control-character syntax, which JavaScript regexes do not support. `/[\^@-\^H\u000b-\^_\u007f]/g` parses as the ranges U+0040–U+005E and U+000B–U+005E plus U+005F/U+007F, so every space, digit, uppercase letter, underscore and most punctuation is already replaced by a space before the redaction passes run. Diagnostics are destroyed ("POST /v3/execute failed: 401 Unauthorized" becomes "v execute failed Unauthorized"), the credential patterns for `Authorization:` headers, `Bearer` tokens, JWTs and URL userinfo no longer match on the mangled text (so secrets such as `hunter2` survive as `hunter`), and the test `redacts credentials, headers, tokens and URL userinfo but keeps the diagnostic readable` fails its `toContain('POST /v3/execute failed: 401 Unauthorized')` assertion. Use a real control-character class such as /[\x00-\x08\x0B-\x1F\x7F]/g.

verdict.rationale: Batch 1/1 gera3d/dsh-superagent-prototype#107@2daef8122c24: The boundary wiring, classification, retry/uncertainty policy and allowlists check out: installComposioBoundary is registered on the master, worker (workOnly) and ordinary-Session paths, the worker/main allowlists are unchanged (no MCP name added), the observer binding skips retry-health and routing guard without change, nested successful:false/mixed batches are re-classified, successes are retained, timeouts/lost acknowledgements are reported as unknown with no resend, Retry-After is only a wait floor for unknown outcomes, and the regression suites drive a real ToolRuntime (plus the installed MCP bridge when present). However the new sanitizeDiagnostic control-character strip is malformed: its caret-notation class parses as printable ranges, mangling diagnostics before redaction and defeating header/token/URL-userinfo redaction, and the accompanying sanitization test cannot pass as written. That defect blocks acceptance until fixed.
